silhouette.reason: Eight individually posed arms with curled tips, bulbous warty mantle and the funnel: unmistakably an octopus from every view.
fixes: vary the arm poses more (two arms curled under, one extended) so the TOP view is less like a symmetric star

proportions.reason: 1.3 × 1.4 × 0.5 m for a large adult female; arms are roughly 3× mantle length as in photos, but they stay uniformly thick for most of their length and taper late.
fixes: taper the arms continuously from the web to the tip (anatomy.ts)
enlarge the inter-arm web toward the base

materials.reason: Mottled red-brown skin and pale suckers read, but the whole surface is matte: no wet sheen, no translucency at the thin arm tips.
fixes: lower roughness for a wet skin sheen (skin.ts)
pale, slightly translucent tint at the arm tips and sucker rims

detail.reason: Double sucker rows along every arm, mantle warts, slit-pupil eye; the arms themselves are smooth tubes with no skin folds or papillae.
fixes: papillae and skin folds along the arm tops (detail.ts)
sucker size decreasing toward the tips

wear.reason: Pristine: no missing arm tip, no scars, no colour change across the body.
fixes: one regenerating shorter arm tip and a few healed scars (seeded)

lod.reason: LOD2 (2.1k) keeps the eight arms but the mantle turns blocky and the arm tips break into segments in the far view.
fixes: more rings on the LOD2 mantle and arm tips (~3k total)
move LOD0 triangles from sucker rims on the hidden underside to the mantle
